_comment: Constants and formulas that were previously hardcoded (differently, in several places) across ad hoc scripts. Consolidated here so the whole pipeline and any future game engine reads the same numbers. Expanded to cover the full ruleset (turn order, movement, power modes, alliances, victory) after discovering data/rules.json was only a partial distillation of reference/Global Cataclysm Design Doc.odt -- see docs/GAME_ARCHITECTURE.md for how this maps onto the engine.

setup.stacking_cap_scope: a starting-setup purchase limit only (not an in-game limit): every unit purchased at a territory counts against that territory's cap, including naval units and any air unit riding an Aircraft Carrier's escort, even though those deploy to a sea zone rather than the land territory itself. See production.per_turn_deploy_cap_formula for the separate, ongoing (post-setup) rule.
setup.naval_purchase_rule: naval units may only be purchased at a coastal territory (has >=1 adjacent sea zone) and deploy to that sea zone, not the land territory
setup.no_shared_sea_zones_rule: no two factions may deploy naval units (or carrier-based aircraft) to the same sea zone in the starting setup
setup.excluded_naval_zones_note: sea zone id 43 (Caspian Sea) never hosts a naval deployment, default or override, in any starting-setup scenario
setup.carrier_escort_rule: every purchased Aircraft Carrier must have at least 1 escorting Fighter or Bomber, which deploys to the carrier's own sea zone instead of a land territory
setup.mandatory_land_unit_rule: every land territory with a foreign-faction land neighbor must have at least 1 land unit (Infantry, Mechanized Infantry, or Armor) at setup -- does not need to be specifically Infantry
setup.unit_diversity_rule: each faction must purchase at least 6 of the 8 purchasable unit types in its starting setup; data/factions.json's per-faction 'focus' list guides which types are emphasized (by spend/quantity), not which types are excluded
setup.leftover_budget_rule: spend the full per-faction budget; when there is a small remainder that can't buy a whole new unit, upgrade an existing Infantry to Mechanized Infantry to use it up

turn_order: Purchase: spend budget, choose deployment locations. Units are decided now but do not appear on the board yet.
Combat Move: units move to attack; every combat move must result in an attack.
Combat Resolution: 1 air-superiority round (if triggered) + up to 3 rounds of main combat. See combat section below.
Non-Combat Move: units that did not combat-move (air units are exempt from this restriction, see movement section).
Capture Territory: air units alone cannot capture.

Deploy + Income: purchased units from phase 1 appear on the board now; collect income (based on territories controlled at this point; contested territories contribute to neither side) for next turn's budget; the global recovery/heal check runs now too, over the whole board (see combat.recovery_rule).
Alliances: propose/withdraw -- stubbed no-op for v1, see alliances section below.

combat.air_superiority_trigger: occurs only if both sides in the battle have at least 1 air unit present AND at least one of the two sides has at least 1 Fighter present; two bomber-only air forces facing each other do not trigger it
combat.hit_rule: attack die roll >= target's defense is a hit; the max value on the die always hits, even against a target whose defense exceeds the roll
combat.damage_rule: a hit deals damage equal to the attacker's damage rating. A target normally reachable by the roll (defense <= roll) is always preferred and takes full damage, even if the roll happens to be the die's max value. The max-die-always-hits bypass -- reaching a target whose defense exceeds the roll -- is only used once no normally-reachable target remains, and even then is restricted to the single next-highest defense tier above the roll (see target_selection.fallback_rule; a tougher tier still is never reached), and that bypass hit specifically deals half damage (rounded down): the cost of forcing a hit on an otherwise-unhittable target, not a tax on rolling well.

resolution_order.note: within a round, each side resolves its own units grouped by type in this fixed order, then by attack die size ascending within a type (promotions can give same-type units different dice). Same order applies to attacker and defender.

target_selection.eligible_pool_rule: enemy units in the battle with defense <= the attack roll and HP > 0 (not yet eliminated this round)
target_selection.fallback_rule: if the eligible pool is empty, fall back to the eligible units with the next-lowest defense above the roll. This same fallback pool is what a max-die bypass hit draws from too, not the full standing roster -- a unit whose defense is even higher (a tougher tier still) is excluded either way.
target_selection.weighting_note: an attacking unit is twice as likely to target an eligible enemy unit of its own unit type as any other eligible unit, except a Bomber attacker, which uses uniform (1x) weighting across the whole eligible pool. Bombers themselves are ordinary targets for everyone else's attacks -- no special protection, no extra likelihood.

combat.casualty_resolution: attacker rolls all attacks first (defending casualties noted, not removed), then defender rolls all attacks (both sides' casualties removed together)
combat.progressive_elimination_note: within one side's own ordered roll-through (per resolution_order), damage accumulates progressively against the other side -- a unit-type group resolving later in that same side's sequence can find its preferred targets already reduced to 0 HP by an earlier group in the sequence. Actual removal from the board for BOTH sides happens together only after both attacker and defender have finished rolling for the round.
combat.battle_resolution_pass_note: global across the whole map for a turn's combat resolution step -- every declared sea battle resolves to completion first, then every declared land battle; never interleaved per battle pair. This is what allows surviving transports/escorts from an already-resolved naval battle to continue their combat move into the adjacent land battle before it resolves.
combat.promotion_check_note: promotion is checked after every round of combat, including the air-superiority round -- a mid-battle promotion (die size up, +1 defense) affects that same battle's remaining rounds.
combat.recovery_rule: a unit heals to full HP once a full round has elapsed since it last took part in a round of combat, counting the turn it was hurt on as the start of that count. Tracked against a single global, monotonically-increasing turn counter (one tick per faction-turn, not per round): a unit heals once current_global_turn - last_combat_global_turn >= num_powers, checked at the deploy phase of EVERY faction's turn, over the whole board -- not only the acting faction's own units. Example: a unit damaged during faction X's turn heals at the deploy phase of faction X's NEXT turn (exactly one full round later), provided it hasn't been in combat again since.
combat.contested_territory_rule: if units remain on both sides after 3 rounds, the territory stays with its original owner, contributes no IPC to either side, and only the owner's Infantry may be mustered there until resolved
deferred_combat_bonuses: Infantry 'Dig In': +1 defense when defending -- not yet implemented
Amphibious assault first-round combat bonus for transported land units attacking (none for non-amphibious attackers) -- not yet implemented
Alliance-reclaim first-round combat bonus when retaking territory lost by a former ally -- not yet implemented, depends on alliances

movement.combat_move_destination: a combat move physically relocates the attacking units into the target territory/sea zone, which is what makes it contested -- there is no separate 'declare attack from next door' step
movement.no_mid_battle_retreat: once combat starts resolving there is no retreat: a battle ends in elimination of one side, the defender holding after 3 rounds if the attacker is wiped, or the territory becoming contested after 3 rounds if both sides still have units
movement.contested_land_combat_move_rule: a land unit sitting in an already-contested LAND territory may combat-move to another already-contested land space (press the fight elsewhere), or retreat to a friendly (own or allied) space, but may NOT use a combat move to stage a fresh attack from there into a not-yet-contested enemy space -- that must originate from an uncontested friendly space. This is a land-only concept: sea zones are never owned/controlled by a faction the way land is, so a sea unit leaving a sea zone where a battle just happened moves under the ordinary combat-move rules, unrestricted.
movement.enemy_occupation_stop_rule: a land or sea combat move that enters a territory/sea zone occupied by a NON-ALLY (i.e. has non-allied defending units present) must stop there -- it cannot chain through to a further destination in the same move. Own and allied territory is always freely transitable regardless of contested status. Transports never count as an occupying presence for this check (a zone with only enemy Transports in it doesn't block passage). Air units are exempt entirely and may fly over enemy-held territory freely, in either the combat-move or non-combat-move phase.
movement.empty_foreign_territory_rule: a combat move CAN pass through and capture an empty (undefended) foreign land territory rather than stopping there -- but only Mechanized Infantry has this ability; every other land/sea unit type stops upon entering ANY foreign territory, empty or occupied, same as the enemy_occupation_stop_rule. Mechanized Infantry itself still stops on an OCCUPIED foreign territory as normal -- the exception is for empty ones only, and is bounded by its own remaining move budget like any other move, not a separately-limited ability.
movement.noncombat_move_destination: own or allied territory (contested or not -- always legal for land/sea pass-through and stopping), or any territory already contested regardless of who owns it or who's contesting it (unqualified -- not limited to the mover's own contest). Never a clean (uncontested), non-allied foreign land territory. A sea zone occupied by a non-ally blocks non-combat movement entirely (that would require a combat move instead) -- an allied warship's presence does not. Air units follow a different, stricter landing rule -- see air_landing_rule.
movement.air_landing_rule: a non-combat air move must end on own-or-allied land (contested or not -- landing there doesn't care about contested status either way, unlike ground pass-through rules) or specifically the mover's OWN aircraft carrier -- never an ally's carrier, even though an ally's land is fine. A combat air move must end on a real attack target -- non-ally-occupied territory, or already contested (joining the fight) -- own/allied territory isn't an attack, and neither is empty foreign territory, since air alone can't capture (per turn_order's Capture Territory phase); there's nothing there to actually attack.
movement.combat_or_noncombat_not_both: non-air units (land and sea) may combat-move OR non-combat-move in a turn, never both. Air units are the sole exception and may always make a non-combat move too, even after already making a combat move the same turn -- the two aren't mutually exclusive for air the way they are for everyone else.
movement.alliance_note: FactionState.alliance (see alliances section below) is now actively consulted by movement legality -- own-or-allied territory/units are treated as friendly/non-blocking throughout this section -- even though full alliance MECHANICS (joining, withdrawing, betrayal, the reclaim bonus) remain out of scope for v1. See alliances.status.
movement.water_movement_bonus_rule: a land unit that begins its turn in a sea zone, OR enters a sea zone at any point during its current move (becoming Transport cargo -- one transport per unit), gets a flat +1 added to BOTH its combat_move and non_combat_move stat for the rest of that turn. This applies dynamically/retroactively: as soon as the unit touches water mid-move, its remaining hop budget for the move in progress extends by 1 -- e.g. Infantry (combat_move 1) can combat-move onto adjacent water then continue onto adjacent land, because entering the water grants the +1 that pays for the second hop. A Mechanized Infantry that begins its turn already in water can move 3 spaces that turn (base 2 + 1). There is no separate per-hop cost to board or disembark -- this flat bonus is the whole model.
movement.transport_amphibious: surviving transports (and the land units they carry) can continue a combat move into adjacent land after winning/surviving the naval battle, only possible because sea battles resolve before land battles (see combat.battle_resolution_pass_order). A transported unit's Transport is destroyed with it if sunk. Transported units don't earn XP. A land unit in transit may move THROUGH a HOSTILE sea zone -- one that's either occupied (enemy combatants present) or already contested (an unresolved battle there) -- specifically to reach adjacent land, but not to chain onward into a further, more open sea zone beyond that. The land reached this way can be enemy territory (an attack), an empty foreign territory (a capture), a territory already contested (joining the fight), OR the mover's own friendly territory (landing safely to escape the hostile water) -- landing is always a legal way to end the move regardless of whose land it is, and it's still classified as a combat move even when it ends on friendly soil, since it's the act of crossing hostile water that requires one, not the destination. Completing the crossing is contingent on the unit surviving that sea zone's naval battle first, since it lands only after the battle resolves, not before or regardless of the outcome.
movement.neutral_exclusion: NEUTRAL territories are excluded from every legal move/attack target entirely -- not enterable, not attackable

production.cap_scope: a pure unit-COUNT limit on newly-deployed units per territory per turn -- not IPC-weighted, and distinct from setup.territory_stacking_cap_formula (which only applies at initial setup). There is no cap at all on total units already present in a territory -- only on how many new ones can land there in a single turn.

promotion.effect: permanent combat bonus: attack die steps up one size (max D12), +1 defense (max 10), +1 HP
promotion.demotion: not specified in the current design doc revision
promotion.service_record_note: every unit is tracked as an individual, persistent record (stable unit_id), not an anonymous stack count -- its XP, promotion status, and current damage/HP all persist on that specific unit across turns and battles.

power_modes.human_bot: functionally identical to the engine -- both get full turns through the same order-submission API, full budget/production; differ only in who/what submits orders
power_modes.defensive: seeded via the 100-IPC/no-SC scenario ruleset (see data/scenarios/starting_setup_100ipc.json). Never receives a turn: no purchases, no movement, no reinforcement, can't join alliances. Its territory IS capturable and its starting units DO fight back normally as an ordinary defender when attacked.
power_modes.neutral: zero units, zero turns. Its territory is a hard exclusion from every other power's legal move/attack targets -- not a combatant, an impassable region.

alliances.status: partially implemented for v1: FactionState.alliance is a plain membership tag (two factions are allied if it's set and equal) that MOVEMENT rules actively consult -- own-or-allied territory/units count as friendly throughout the movement section above. What's still out of scope: the alliance MECHANICS themselves -- no join/withdraw flow, no betrayal/contested-on-betrayal, no allied combat bonus, no allied-defense-together in combat resolution. Something (a scenario setup, a test, or a future engine.py API) has to set FactionState.alliance directly; there's no in-game action that changes it yet.
alliances.design_doc_reference: 2 or 3 powers can join in alliances depending on game settings. Can withdraw from an alliance OR invite 1 power to join at turn end; invited power immediately accepts or rejects. Can't withdraw while you have units in an allied Strategic Center. Occupied former-ally territories become contested; the former ally gets a combat bonus in the first round of combat to reclaim them. Allies can move through each other's territories without claiming them; their units don't fight each other. When attacking a space contested by other powers, the attacker chooses which non-aligned power they're attacking. Allies defend together.

victory.elimination_rule: a power is eliminated when it controls <=1 Strategic Center (original or captured); contested SCs still count as controlled. Remove all remaining units from the board on elimination.
victory.game_end_rule: the game ends when there are no unallied powers remaining

map.adjacency_source: Delaunay triangulation over territory center points (computed on a cylinder: the map wraps east-west, x=3500 is the same seam as x=0, so triangulation uses ghost copies of every point shifted by the map width; north-south does not wrap), edges kept under a 420px length threshold, plus a small hand-confirmed FORCED_EDGES list in tools/compute_adjacency.py for real adjacencies that threshold would otherwise wrongly exclude. Fully regenerable -- see tools/compute_adjacency.py. Every space in territories.json is a real graph node; there is no fallback category for territories added later.
map.foreign_neighbor_flag_definition: a land territory has at least one land neighbor belonging to a different faction
